title: Sausage pasta with Jerusalem artichokes and sage

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Sausages, dried pasta, Parmesan, fresh vegetables and herbs are all things a grandparent would keep.

supermarket.reason: Jerusalem artichokes, cavolo nero, sausages and penne are all stocked at mainstream supermarkets in winter at everyday prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a saucepan and a colander, and the techniques are simple frying and boiling.

works.reason: 400g artichokes, six sausages and 350g pasta with cavolo nero makes a well-balanced, well-seasoned dinner for four.

honest_times.reason: The steps run 10 minutes plus 8 minutes of frying before the pasta is even put on to boil, so the real cook time is nearer 30 minutes than the printed 20, and scrubbing and thinly slicing 400g of knobbly artichokes also strains the 15-minute prep for a quick dinner.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including sage, chilli, lemon and Parmesan, is used, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Golden fried Jerusalem artichokes with sausage and cavolo nero suit late January, and the artichokes are a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family pasta with protein and two vegetables.
